useLayoutEffect runs synchronously after React updates the DOM but before the browser paints, while useEffect runs after paint. Reach for useLayoutEffect only when you must read layout (measure with getBoundingClientRect, scroll position) and then change state or the DOM before the user sees a frame, e.g. positioning a tooltip, to avoid a flicker; for everything else use useEffect since layout effects block painting (and warn on the server in SSR setups).

Yes, there's a real difference. structuredClone keeps Dates, Maps, Sets, typed arrays and handles circular references, while the JSON round trip turns Dates into strings, Maps/Sets into {}, drops undefined and functions, and throws on cycles. Neither copies functions or class prototypes, and structuredClone is available on Node 18.

`as const` changes the inferred type: literals stay literal and everything becomes readonly, but nothing is checked. `satisfies` checks the value against a type without changing its inferred type, so you catch typos but keep the precise type. Use both together (`as const satisfies Config`) to get a checked, literal, readonly value.

`using` declares a resource that is disposed automatically when the scope exits, by calling its [Symbol.dispose]() method (or await using with [Symbol.asyncDispose]()), even if an error is thrown, and disposal runs in reverse order of declaration. It needs TS 5.2+ and a runtime that has Symbol.dispose, so check our Node target before relying on it.
